scope: Five target cardiac families in AccessGUDID; all results of four single-term searches plus three narrowed EMPOWER searches retrieved. Inclusion requires matching labeler and brand or description; unrelated keyword matches excluded.

methods.interpretation: Five target cardiac families in AccessGUDID; all results of four single-term searches plus three narrowed EMPOWER searches retrieved. Inclusion requires matching labeler and brand or description; unrelated keyword matches excluded.

44 accepted primary-DI records, representing 36 exact labeler/model pairs. Repeated model labels across DIs retained. Package identifiers remain nested in source identifiers, not promoted to separate model rows.

All 48 candidate primary DIs resolved through official v3 lookup; model, labeler and public record UUID matched to search results. Four unrelated candidates excluded. No manufacturer catalog or paper values imported.

Search page_size=100 used to retrieve complete small result sets in one response and avoid order changes across default 10-row pages. Search output is a current bounded snapshot, not a global census of aliases or unpublished investigational products.

No target cardiac pacemaker verified by EMPOWER AND pacemaker, EMPOWER AND leadless, or EMPOWER AND Boston Scientific. The Boston result is unrelated LithoVue Empower equipment. No-hit queries do not prove worldwide absence or a regulatory decision.

Publication/version/distribution-end dates are GUDID fields, not original clearance or approval dates. Five accepted AVEIR records first published after February 2024 are flagged. Current fields on older records are not reconstructed historical values.

companyName is GUDID labeler. ST. JUDE MEDICAL, INC. is retained rather than replaced by Abbott. Distribution status is source-reported, not an independent approval, recall, safety or present sales determination.

GMDN implantability plus term/description used for explicit component-role annotation. 18 active implanted DI records, 3 implanted lead DI records, and 23 nonimplanted equipment/accessory/software records. These are record counts, not distinct technologies.

Three EMBLEM lead records describe subcutaneous electrodes but carry the generic GMDN name Endocardial defibrillation lead. Preserve both, flag the discrepancy; do not classify them as endocardial implants from GMDN wording alone.

UDI identity expansion does not establish AI. Prior BIOMONITOR IV external SmartECG conclusion is not extended to other family members or to onboard execution. Other prior AI assessments remain separate and unchanged.

Six new US UDI sheets precede 18 earlier sheets. Chinese 48-model expansion and five-model resolution remain intact. US expansion includes previously captured BIOMONITOR IV DI; 43 other accepted US DIs are new relative to the original repository snapshot.

gmdn.gmdnPTDefinition: A battery-powered, hermetically-sealed pulse generator impregnated with a steroid (e.g., dexamethasone) intended to be implanted with a catheter, via transvenous access, into the right ventricle (i.e., single-chamber pacing) of an arrhythmic heart to generate/conduct electrical impulses to improve cardiac output. It contains sensors to detect changes in the body (e.g., motion, breathing frequency) and to adjust the pacing rate accordingly (rate-responsive). Wireless telemetry with external devices enables programming adjustments and may allow on-going heart monitoring; it does not provide defibrillation therapy. Disposable devices associated with implantation may be included.

gmdn.gmdnPTDefinition: An assembly of devices designed to analyse the performance of an implanted pacemaker based on electrocardiographic measurements that can be monitored transtelephonically. It typically includes a computer-based pacemaker analyser, a 12-lead electrocardiograph (ECG), and a transtelephonic receiver and/or transmitter. It provides data taken directly from the patient (e.g., ECG electrodes are applied to the patient and a test magnet is placed over the pacemaker to activate it) or a pacemaker programmer. Signals are sent to the receiver where pacemaker function information is displayed. This system may also include a database that collects and stores patient data.

Pacemaker communication and ECG data collection is achieved via the patient cable/electrodes which are typically included. The device is intended to be used by a healthcare professional in a clinical setting.

gmdn.gmdnPTDefinition: An external device intended to enable a healthcare professional in a clinical setting to noninvasively change the settings of, and extract data from, an implanted cardiac pulse generator (e.g., pacemaker, pacemaker/defibrillator). It includes a radio-frequency transmitter/receiver and may be intended to operate independently or in conjunction with a personal computer (PC)/tablet using dedicated software.

gmdn.gmdnPTDefinition: An implantable flexible wire with an electrode, insulated with non-conductive material except at its ends, intended to function as an electrical conductor to transmit defibrillation impulses from an implanted cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) [automatic implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (AICD)] to the endocardium of the right ventricle. It may also be intended to transmit pacing impulses from a cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) pulse generator, AICD, or other pacing device. It is typically impregnated with a steroid (e.g., dexamethasone) intended to elute into the tissues to reduce inflammation.

gmdn.gmdnPTDefinition: An implantable pulse generator (IPG) with a cardiac rhythm recognition system, to analyse an electrocardiogram (ECG), intended to deliver an electrical impulse(s) to defibrillate the heart (restore normal rhythm) or slow a rapid heart rate, and typically to pace a slow heart rate. It is implanted in a pouch beneath the skin of the patient's chest or abdomen and has connected a lead(s) that are positioned inside or on one heart chamber (typically right ventricle) to monitor the ECG and to automatically deliver the electrical impulse. It has internal batteries that provide the energy for the discharges; it is commonly known as an automatic implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (AICD).

gmdn.gmdnPTDefinition: A sterile hand-held manual surgical instrument designed to create a tunnel (an artificial passageway) through subcutaneous tissue for the placement of an implantable extracardiac lead/electrode. It is a long, thin, semi-flexible rod with a rounded distal tip and a handle at the proximal end to allow the surgeon to push through body tissues; it may include an integrated sheath (e.g., split sheath) intended to assist lead placement. This is a single-use device.

gmdn.gmdnPTDefinition: A device designed specifically to be attached to the handle (or holding portion) of a surgical instrument to provide grip for improved manipulation of the handle during surgical procedures. It is typically a synthetic polymer device designed for attachment to a handle and is not intended to provide a physical sterile barrier between the handle and the hand of a healthcare professional (i.e., not a handle cover). This is a single-use device.
